result.narrative:
Arcline Fabrications NV is showing consistent signs of liquidity stress. Nordhaven Trade Credit (CL05) reports six open invoices totalling EUR 559,900, the worst of them INV000075 at 45 days past due for EUR 145,600. There is no settled invoice history on file, so the internal ledger offers no payment trend, but external reporting fills the gap: vendors described settlement delays of 60-100 days against 45-day terms in November 2025, two lenders opened a review of their working capital exposure after a cash credit enhancement was not sanctioned in full, and by March 2026 workers at the Antwerp plant had stopped work over part-paid wages and provident fund deductions that were not remitted.

The score is 63.3, in the High Risk band, from 0.65 x 70.0 on the payment leg (45 DPD, weighted 45.5) plus 0.35 x 50.9 on the news leg (weighted 17.8). Only the severity-5 wage delay item NWS0007 scores; three further severity-4 items decay to 24.55, 24.79 and 25.41 and contribute nothing, so the band is if anything conservative. The adjudicator agreed with caveats. Those caveats matter here: the payment leg rests on a single delinquency with no internal baseline and holds only because the external reporting corroborates it; NWS0005 names "Arcline Inds." with no Antwerp location and matches the insured only on sector, so it should not be leaned on until the legal entity is confirmed; and all news evidence, at 204, 319, 314 and 301 days old, predates the current delinquency with nothing later confirming whether the wage arrears were resolved.

The recommendation is to REDUCE the Nordhaven limit from EUR 820,000 to EUR 559,900, which brings expected loss from EUR 365,779 to EUR 249,755 against the 25% appetite at a PD of 0.5831. In practice this caps the line at current drawn exposure and stops new drawdown. The adjudicator flags that the EUR 820k limit was last reviewed in Oct 2024 and is materially stale against the deterioration evidenced since November 2025, and that open exposure already sits at about 68% of it; the limit should be re-underwritten rather than merely trimmed. Note also the buy-while-delaying pattern reported in NWS0004 — fresh orders placed through the period of stretched payables — which the formula does not capture and which points to exposure growing ahead of the next review.

To move down, the score needs to fall 3.3 points below 60.0 to reach Watch. News alone does not hold the band, so curing the payment leg is the lever: settlement of INV000075 and a clean run of paid invoices that establishes a trend in place of the current "insufficient_history" flag. A news refresh confirming the March 2026 wage and provident fund arrears were cleared, and confirmation of whether NWS0005 concerns this legal entity at all, would both firm up the picture before renewal.
